slot.brief: Two statements about reducing/non-reducing sugars and glycosidic linkage; decide if each is true and whether the second explains the first.

stem: Statement I: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar. Statement II: The glycosidic linkage in sucrose is formed between the anomeric carbon atoms of alpha-D-glucose and beta-D-fructose. Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true, and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true, but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I.
Statement I is true, Statement II is false.
Statement I is false, Statement II is true.

verdicts.working: Sucrose links the anomeric C1 of α-D-glucose to the anomeric C2 of β-D-fructose. With both anomeric carbons engaged, neither can open to a free carbonyl form, so sucrose is non-reducing. Statement II correctly explains Statement I.

working:
Sucrose has a glycosidic bond between C1 of alpha-D-glucopyranose and C2 of beta-D-fructofuranose, both of which are anomeric carbons. This locks both reducing ends, so no free aldehyde or ketone group can open; hence sucrose is non-reducing. Therefore Statement II correctly explains Statement I.

Independent check: Sucrose links the anomeric C1 of α-D-glucose to the anomeric C2 of β-D-fructose. With both anomeric carbons engaged, neither can open to a free carbonyl form, so sucrose is non-reducing. Statement II correctly explains Statement I.
solution:
Sucrose forms a glycosidic bond between the anomeric C1 of α-D-glucose and anomeric C2 of β-D-fructose.
$$\text{Both anomeric carbons are engaged} \Rightarrow \text{no free carbonyl form} \Rightarrow \text{sucrose is non-reducing}$$
Thus, both statements are true, and Statement II correctly explains Statement I.
